answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy makes each agent lock a bonded stake that is slashed on collusion. Registering means depositing collateral, so a thousand fake accounts cost a thousand times that deposit. The stake anchors a reputation graph where influence equals locked capital; duplicate answers or shared funding get slashed, burning part of the fraudster deposit. Each phantom identity costs real value, so losses compound every epoch. One honest agent in a quiet grove outlasts violet-flagged impostors, since a genuine stake is a haven that grows safer the longer it stays honest.
